Just like christmas, easter was in fact an originally pagan holiday. This got me thinking, does christianity have any original holidays to offer, that weren't derived from another belief system?
Does christianity have any original holidays?

I never really understood how Christmas is somehow considered a stolen holiday from Pagans. Christmas was placed around the same Pagan holiday to replace it on the calendar. Most likely, Christmas was strategically placed but I don't think that doesn't make it "original". It does not represent the original Pagan holiday very well. The same goes for Easter. I believe Easter is a pretty original holiday as it takes place during the period when Jesus was crucified. The focus on Easter was his resurrection, though public display of Easter would pretty much paint a picture of Easter being about Spring and bunnies and eggs or whatever. You might find silly things like egg hunts at a church during Easter, but in no way does that represent what is being preached on the pulpit every year. And actually, Easter takes place during the Jewish holiday Passover every year as a part of one of Jesus's predictions and fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy (Isaiah 53:7, I Corinthians 5:7). I haven't researched how old the Pagan Easter is, but Passover I would bet predates the pagan tradition. (I am just guessing here and too lazy to do the research right now :P)

However, Christmas is not mentioned anywhere in the Bible. So some Christians do not recognize it as a holiday anyway. Neither is Easter, Thanksgiving, Valentines Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day, Independence Day, etc.

Traditional things mentioned in the Bible, like the Lord's Supper, are very commonly practiced on a monthly or weekly basis. Most holidays traditionally practiced within the church that are mentioned in the Bible are Advent, Lent, Good Friday, Palm Sunday, and Ash Wednesday. Other Holidays created by the church are All Saints Day, St. Andrews, St. Patricks, (not sure bout Valentines), Reformation Day, and Boxing day.

Anyway, Hope this helps!
